conviction_note: A storm-free Florida Q3, plus the first full quarter of a reinsurance program the company says costs double digits less on a risk-adjusted basis, makes a large EPS beat on the $0.84 bar and a mechanical raise of the FY net-income guide ($455-470M, against $274.4M already earned in H1) likely. The market can see all of this: the stock is up 29% in October and 34% since Q2. Its own beats have bought -9.1/-1.1/+9.7/-2.4/+3.5. Peer UVE printed net income +32% and rose only 0.9%. Short interest has risen into the print. So p_up is 52 on an abs move of 5.5, and the findings sum to about +0.1. The two measurements agree that this is close to a non-result.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS $0.84 (AAII/estimate-revisions page dated 2026-10-27, 5 analysts: https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/522576-what-you-need-to-know-about-slide-insurance-holdings-incs-q3-earnings). Consistent with MarketBeat FY2026 consensus EPS $3.84 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/SLDE/earnings/), which less H1 actual $2.08 leaves $1.76 for H2. Older Benzinga tables show $0.59-0.65 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SLDE/earnings-forecasts), predating upward revisions. Company guide: FY2026 net income $455-470M, GWP $1.85-1.95B, reaffirmed 2026-07-28 (https://finviz.com/news/373710/slide-reports-second-quarter-2026-results). print_vs_bar is my estimate of Q3 EPS around $1.10-1.30 against $0.84, an inference from peer and cat data, not a document.
positioning_check: Short interest 7,413,569 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 5.91 days to cover, up from 6,445,149 on 2026-08-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/slde/short-interest). That is 6.3% of 116.8M shares outstanding and roughly 10-11% of float, if Lucas-controlled shares (~46.2M per an April 2026 Form 4 report, https://www.placera.se/telegram/slide-insurance-slide-insurance-holdings-insider-sold-shares-worth-2-307-975-according-to-a-recent-sec-filing-20260423) are excluded. Shorts are moderately sized and were building into the print. Skew: not available, because the chain is unusable (ATM spread 160% of mid, OI 482). Put/call OI is 0.72. Tape: +27.8% over 20 days, +5.2% over 5 days, 1.1% off the 52-week high, spot $28.75, above the ~$24 average analyst target (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SLDE/sentiment) and near Barclays' $31.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was storm-free in Florida. No named storm made Florida landfall July-September (Bertha and Edouard hit LA/TX, and the first hurricane of the season, Isaias, came on Oct 9). It was also the first full quarter of the 2026-27 cat program, which Slide says carries a double-digit risk-adjusted rate cut. Peer Universal (UVE), reporting 2026-10-22, showed Q3 net income +31.8% to $52.5M, net loss ratio -5.6 pts to 64.6% and ceded premium ratio 27.6% vs 32.7%. Slide's Q3 2025 analogue earned $111M at a 48.5% CR with a smaller book; Q2 2026 earned $134.9M (EPS $1.06). A Q3 2026 EPS of about $1.10-1.30 against the $0.84 bar is likely. With $274.4M of H1 net income against a $455-470M FY guide that implies only $181-196M for all of H2, a clean Q3 makes a raise to the FY net-income guide near-mechanical.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SLDE has beaten EPS consensus 5 of 5 times by $0.16-0.36 (MarketBeat table). Reactions: Q2'25 -9.14%, Q3'25 -1.07% (+$0.30 beat), Q4'25 +9.68% (+$0.36 beat with the first FY2026 guide), Q1'26 -2.44% (+$0.20), Q2'26 +3.46% (+$0.18, guide only reaffirmed). Peer UVE beat ~$1.08 consensus by a wide margin on 2026-10-22 and closed +0.91% on 10-23 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uve/history/). The one large up-move followed a guidance event.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock went from $22.31 on Sep 30 to ~$28.75 (+29%) as the season stayed quiet, and rose +2.9% on UVE's print day. What may remain unpriced is the size of a FY guide raise: consensus FY EPS of $3.84 (~$488M) already sits above the $470M guide top, so a raise only to ~$490M would add nothing, while a raise to $520M+ would. If the market had fully priced a large raise, the stock would trade above the $28-31 top analyst targets, and the targets have not moved since early October.
findings.independence: Separate sources: Slide's own guide and H1 numbers (https://finviz.com/news/373710/slide-reports-second-quarter-2026-results); its reinsurance renewal, a double-digit risk-adjusted decrease (https://www.artemis.bm/news/slide-renews-5-463bn-of-total-aggregate-reinsurance-limit-first-event-capacity-hits-3-98bn/); and season data showing no Florida landfall in Q3 (https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/weather/2026/07/24/tropics-so-far-in-2026). The UVE print is a peer proxy, not Slide's own number.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias (Cat 2, Destin, 2026-10-09) is a Q4 loss event that management will likely size on the Oct 28 8:30 ET call. Florida OIR puts statewide insured losses at $582M and 46,509 claims as of Oct 15, 79% in Santa Rosa and Escambia. AM Best calls it an 'earnings event'. UVE's CEO said claims were 'less significant than initially anticipated'. Slide does not report to OIR market-intelligence data, so its own count is unknown. Its retention is $166.8M first event, so any loss is fully net and offsets part of a guide raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior post-IPO hurricane disclosure for Slide. The stock moved -0.63% on 2026-10-09, landfall day, and has since risen ~14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock barely reacted at landfall, and industry estimates have fallen since (Cotality $2-3bn, below pre-landfall estimates). It is unpriced only if Slide's Panhandle share turns out larger than assumed. A priced worry would show as a post-landfall drawdown, and there was none.
findings.independence: Proxy: statewide and peer data, nothing Slide-specific. A different source on industry size: https://beinsure.com/news/hurricane-isaias-triggers-insurance-claims-582mn-in-florida/ (2026-10-19). UVE's 'less than anticipated' comment is in https://www.reinsurancene.ws/universals-q326-revenues-rise-9-6-to-439m/, the same document as finding 1.

findings.finding: Top-line momentum is fading. Policies in force were flat sequentially (508,928 at Q1 to 509,075 at Q2) as Citizens takeouts slowed to bind reinsurance. Average premium per residential policy fell to $3,614 from $3,964 y/y. Citizens itself had shrunk to ~274k policies by June 2026, so the takeout pool that drove Q4'25 GPW +56.7% is nearly exhausted. Florida's 30-day average homeowners rate request is -4.8%. Q3 GPW is therefore likely flat to down against Q3'25's $463.4M. This lands largely inside the GWP guide of $1.85-1.95B, which against H1's $922.8M implies H2 of $927M-1.03B versus $1.08B in H2'25, down 5-14%. It is a risk for any 2027 growth commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'25 (-9.14%) and Q3'25 (-1.07%) both missed revenue estimates ($261.6M vs $271.2M; $265.7M vs $279.4M) while beating EPS. Q2'26 beat revenue ($386.8M vs $370.8M) and rose +3.46%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The guide already implies an H2 GPW decline, and the coverager piece frames diversification as 'a 2027 story'. What would not be priced is 2027 commentary that confirms Florida shrinkage before the new states contribute. If the market were focused on it, analyst targets would lag the stock less and the multiple would sit below the 7.1x it holds against an industry median of 11.6x.
findings.independence: Citizens count from a separate source: https://www.citizensfla.com/es/-/20260623-smaller-citizens-secures-coverage-for-2026-hurricane-season (2026-06-23). Rate requests: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/property/florida-approves-more-home-insurance-rate-cuts-as-doubledigit-requests-pile-up-591320.aspx (2026-09-27). The PIF figures come from the Q1 8-K and the Q2 summaries.

findings.finding: Positioning runs into the print. The stock is +27.8% over 20 days, 1.1% off its 52-week high and above the ~$24 consensus target. Short interest rose from 6.45M (Aug 31) to 7.41M shares (Oct 15, 5.9 days to cover, ~10-11% of float). Peer UVE's clean beat bought only +0.9%. Sell-the-news risk on a good print is partly offset by squeeze fuel if the guide raise is large.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a +11.6% run between Q1 and Q2 (per unusualwhales as of Oct 6, for the period since the last print), Q2's beat bought +3.46%. The Q1'26 beat was sold at -2.44%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is not a missed fact. It is filed so the judges see that the run-up and rising shorts set the bar for the reaction. Had the run-up been viewed as stretched, short interest would have stopped growing or targets would have been cut. Instead both shorts and targets crept up.
findings.independence: Prices from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/slde/history/. The peer reaction is from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uve/history/.

findings.finding: There is capital-return capacity for the call: $114.1M remained on the repurchase program at Q2. H1 buybacks were about $191M, at ~$17.75-17.95 a share, and the initial dividend is $0.07. Debt-to-cap is 2.4%, and a storm-free Q3 adds ~$130-150M of earnings. A new authorization or a dividend step-up is plausible but not announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend initiation with Q2 coincided with +3.46%. There is no separate history.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference with no announcement. Buybacks look less accretive at $28.75 than at $18, so the market may not expect an upsized program.
findings.independence: Buyback total and debt-to-cap from https://www.panabee.com/news/slide-earnings-q2-2026-report. Inference only.

outside_window.finding: The 2027 reinsurance renewal (June 1, 2027) and geographic diversification (NJ, RI, NY launch, California E&S) are framed by management as a 2027 story. No resolution inside the window beyond call commentary.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the run-up: a clean quarter and a likely guide raise are what the +28% 20-day move has been pricing. With no usable skew and short interest building, nothing found says the market under-priced this print, so the lean is barely positive.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): SLDE has beaten 5 of 5 with reactions of -9.1 to +9.7, and peer UVE's beat bought +0.9%. The Q3 beat / guide-raise finding went from +1.5 to +1.0 and p_up from 53 to 52.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the GWP guide already implies an H2 decline of 5-14% y/y, so a weak Q3 GPW lands inside it. The top-line finding went from -0.8 to -0.4.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to the company FY guide plus two agreeing estimate sources (AAII $0.84; MarketBeat FY $3.84). Older Benzinga numbers were rejected, and no cap was applied.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest was looked up (~10-11% of float, building). It is not crowded at the 18-23% level, so the positioning finding stays at -0.5 and is not shrunk further.
Left standing: Isaias -0.2 (a proxy, already small) and capital return +0.2 (an inference, small).
